
=================================================================
#50 Jiabeng (駕崩)  (649 July)
Arc: The Chunchu Era · place: changan · tone: imperial deathbed drama
Logline: The empire does not wait for grief to finish its sentence.
=================================================================
[0] ── SCENE: The Cuiwei Palace ──
[1] ¶ Two summers earlier, the Son of Heaven is dying the way he did everything else: in front of witnesses.
[2] ¶ The crown prince holds a hand that used to lift a lamp to stone horses. It has nothing left to lift. It still gives orders.
[3] The Second Emperor: Zhi. / The six. When they go up the mountain— / Put the purple one nearest the door. …He hates waiting.
[4] The Third Emperor: I know, Father. You told me. You’ve told me every—
[5] ¶ The emperor dies in the Cuiwei Palace in the fifth month. He is fifty-one. The room is kept too warm, and the silk on the bed is the colour of late wheat.
[6] [TERM Jiabeng (駕崩): “The carriage collapses.” Nobody in Chang’an may say the emperor died. Kings die. The Son of Heaven’s carriage simply falls, and the whole empire is meant to hear it land.]
[7] ¶ The crown prince has been sitting since before dawn. He is twenty-one. He has the shoulders for the armour and not yet the face for the title. When the breathing stops, he does not move for a long time — long enough that the ministers begin to look at one another instead of at the bed.
[8] The Third Emperor: ……Father. / Not yet——
[9] ¶ Someone touches his elbow. Someone else is already writing. The empire does not wait for grief to finish its sentence.
[10] ¶ The court kneels, and the young man rises — the same hands that would not leave the bed now accepting the seal, the edict, the yellow silk that means the West has a new centre.
[11] The Third Emperor: I receive the late emperor’s last command. / From this day—— / ……We will listen.
[12] [CARD The Third Emperor]
[13] ¶ He does not say _I_. He says the word that empties a man of his own name. The hall answers like a single throat.
[14] ¶ The will is long on mourning and short on everything else, except one line, which the new emperor reads twice. The war in Liaodong is to stop.
[15] ¶ The great emperor is given a temple name — **Taizong**. The clerks write it in the register and close the book.
[16] ❝QUOTE (Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 22, Goguryeo Annals — King Bojang, yr. 8 (649)): Eighth year, summer, fourth month: Taizong* of Tang died. His testamentary edict called off the Liaodong campaign.❞
[17] ¶ The empire is told how to grieve. The edict fixes the days of mourning by rank, and at dusk in every ward of Chang’an the ward chief walks the lanes and listens at the doors, to be sure the weeping inside is of the proper length.
[18] ¶ Two of his dragons, the Red and the White, both of them Turks, petition to be killed and laid beside him, to guard the tomb the way the six stone horses will. It is the highest loyalty the steppe knows. The court is moved. The young emperor reads the petition twice.
[19] The Third Emperor: Denied. / …Father already has six horses waiting at his door. / He would scold Us for wasting two good generals.
[20] ── SCENE: Surabol ──
[21] ¶ The news crosses the sea in the eighth month. In Surabol, Chunchu reads the will through to the line about Liaodong, and then reads that line again.
[22] King Muyeol: He made me promise to finish it. / And then he left orders to stop. / …Very well. Then it is mine.
[23] ── SCENE: Back at Cuiwei ──
[24] ¶ In an anteroom a young concubine waits with the other women who must not be seen grieving too loudly. Her name is not yet heavy. Her attention already is. She watches how a seal moves from a dead hand to a living one — and files the lesson where ambition keeps its dry goods.
[25] Wu Zetian: (soft, to no one) / So that is how an empire changes owners. / Quietly. With someone else speaking the first sentence.
[26] ¶ The late emperor’s women who bore him no children are sent to the Ganye Temple, to shave their heads and pray for him for the rest of their lives. Wu goes with them.
[27] ── SCENE: Ganye Temple ──
[28] ¶ A year later, on the anniversary, the new emperor comes to the temple to burn incense for his father. A nun in grey looks up at him from the second row, and does not look down again.
[29] The Third Emperor: Lady Wu. / …They cut your hair.
[30] Wu Zetian: Hair grows back, Majesty. / (and already the room tilts a degree toward her)
[31] ¶ **Seven years of a polite queen and a busy nephew. Sooner or later, Silla has to admit who's really sitting in the chair…!**
